errors.text: The proposed BCC+B2 constitution is not a dual-phase solid-solution structure: B2 is an ordered intermetallic phase, directly conflicting with the requested avoidance of intermetallic formation.
No cited evidence demonstrates B2 precipitation, spinodal decomposition, or an Nb-rich/Ti-rich ordered phase in equimolar Nb-Ta-Ti-V after HPT or aging.

The most composition-relevant evidence, E3, instead shows Nb25Ta25Ti25V25 remains a single BCC solid solution after prolonged treatment at 1200°C and is phase-stable through 900°C, undermining the asserted 400–600°C B2 precipitation and above-700°C Laves instability.
Evidence from Cr-containing HfMoTaTiZr, WVTaTi-Cr, and AlCoCrFeNi is transferred to a Cr-, Hf-, Mo-, Al-, Co-, Fe-, and Ni-free Nb-Ta-Ti-V alloy without a thermodynamic or experimental basis.
The falsification experiment does not distinguish grain-boundary or precipitation strengthening from simple solid-solution strengthening because it lacks matched grain-size and phase-state controls.
